tasks.short: Plan, organize and maintain dental health programs

steps.what: Gather programme needs and prepare dental health service and resource summaries
Plan dental health programs and agree priorities, activities and clinical responsibilities
Organize programme activities and maintain the action schedule and status

tasks.design: Use native reports in {OTHER}, the dental service record system, and shared schedules in {PROJECT} and {CALENDAR}. The dentist retains programme priorities, clinical responsibilities and exception coordination while reducing table assembly and repeated schedule updates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service summaries and programme dates can be maintained across separate files and messages.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting and shared action schedules can reuse checked records.
tasks.still_hard: Selecting appropriate services and resolving resource conflicts requires local judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The dentist balances prevention goals, patient needs and clinical capacity.
tasks.altitude: Less summary and schedule administration; clinical programme authority is unchanged.

reach.learn: Service measures and practical resource planning

evidence.claim: Configured reporting and shared schedules can reduce repeated programme administration; this is an unmeasured model scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is dentist programme planning and coordination, excluding care delivery, educational material creation and other staff's activity work.

Front-desk and clinical processes produce existing service date, activity and resource records through unchanged booking and care documentation. Dentist selects periods, validates summaries and captures unmet needs in s1's10 remaining hours. Dentist produces activity, owner, date and dependency fields in s2; s3's18 remaining hours include checking updates and resolving missing availability manually.
Test native reports and calendar configuration first. No new patient profiling or staff scoring is introduced.
research_questions: Do shared summaries and schedules reduce dentist coordination time after exception handling?

already_counted.description: Summary checks and programme coordination exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain report definitions and activity templates

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R78 gives22 gross minus4 upkeep net18. Low assumes only6 hours administration removed;50 hours programme judgement remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Produce and evaluate dental health educational materials

steps.what: Select the dental health topic, audience and reliable clinical source material
Produce dental health educational materials for the selected audience

loop.purpose: Adapt approved dental information into an audience-appropriate draft
loop.input: Verified educational brief, source passages and material template
loop.output: Draft material with source links and stated audience
loop.check: Dentist checks clinical meaning, omissions, risk explanations, readability and consistency with source passages; no personalised advice is invented
loop.stop: One revision then manual production if inaccurate or unsuitable
loop.why_not_simpler: A template places sections but audience-appropriate explanations require semantic rewriting

steps.what: Evaluate accuracy and accessibility and approve the final educational material

tasks.design: Reuse approved templates in {DOCS} before adding a bounded drafting assistant. The dentist selects source content and evaluates the complete material before accepting an exact version; distribution and patient counselling are separate tasks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rewriting accurate clinical content for different audiences takes drafting time.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded text assistant can propose wording from selected source passages.
tasks.still_hard: Plain wording can omit clinically important qualifications.
tasks.human_edge: The dentist judges clinical accuracy and whether the audience can apply the guidance.
tasks.altitude: Less initial writing; clinical editorial responsibility remains human.

reach.learn: Readable explanations and clinical source checks

evidence.claim: Source-bounded text drafting is plausible model capability; no measured dental education-material saving is supplied.

assumptions: Boundary covers producing and evaluating reusable material, excluding individual advice and publishing or mailing it.

Dentist captures topic, audience, purpose, approved source passages and required warnings in s1's30 hours. Missing or conflicting source content triggers manual research and drafting; no unverified structured clinical claim is accepted.
Test native templates first. Evaluation-only cases retain s3 and do not receive hypothetical production savings; shares describe a mixed material-production workload.
unknowns: Source availability and typical material complexity
research_questions: Does drafting reduce total production time after clinical and accessibility evaluation?

already_counted.description: Draft checks and complete final material evaluation

incremental.description: Maintain source versions and review recurring draft errors

approvals.approved_version: Exact final educational text, illustrations if present, source versions and intended audience; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R80 gives20 gross minus4 upkeep net16. Low assumes only5 drafting hours removed due to technical content or evaluation-only workload; source selection30 and final evaluation30 remain full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Less programme administration and first-pass educational writing, with clinical and editorial decisions retained.
reach: Coordinate preventive programmes and material review with dental hygienists
role.ambitious_version: A dentist who organises preventive work and clear educational material with less repeated administration.
